Uncorrected candidate-set cross-entropy, L=−s_positive+logsumexp(s_positive,s_negatives), is a valid sampled ranking objective; it needs no sampling correction when explicitly defined that way. It should not be described as exact full-catalog softmax. Corrections depend on the intended estimator and actual sampling scheme, including inclusion probabilities for sampling without replacement. Corrected sampled softmax generally still has biased finite-sample gradients. [TensorFlow sampling reference](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf), [sampled-softmax analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a/blanc18a.pdf).

For uniform sampling of k unique negatives from an eligible pool of M items, each negative’s inclusion probability is k/M. An importance-weighted denominator estimator is Ẑ=exp(s_positive)+(M/k)Σ exp(s_negative): equivalently, shift negative logits by log(M/k), leaving the always-included positive unchanged. This follows from inclusion weighting; uniformity does not cancel that positive–negative difference. History exclusion gives excluded items zero inclusion probability, so this estimates the denominator over the eligible pool plus positive, not the entire catalog. Specify the exclusion history precisely. Use each example’s actual k and M; mask padded candidates with −∞, average losses over valid targets, and explicitly handle k=0. Variable k changes the uncorrected objective’s difficulty, so report its policy. [Sampling definitions](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf).

Chunking preserves the chosen denominator algebraically: initialize a=s_positive, then update a=logaddexp(a,logsumexp(chunk_logits)); finish with L=a−s_positive. Include every intended candidate exactly once, apply any corrections before reduction, and preserve autograd through every chunk. Separate chunk-wise cross-entropies do not reproduce the global denominator. FP32 accumulation improves stability; exactness is up to floating-point rounding. [PyTorch logsumexp](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.logsumexp.html).
